taxes.combinedRateSource: [VERIFY] Combined 2026 Dallas rate (City of Dallas 0.6988 + Dallas ISD 0.993835 + Dallas County 0.2155 + Dallas College 0.106575 + Parkland Hospital 0.212 per $100). These are jurisdiction-level rates for a City of Dallas / Dallas ISD address; no DCAD record or tax bill was supplied for THIS parcel, so both the rate and the jurisdictions must be confirmed before they are relied on.
taxes.impliedCurrentTaxableValueNote: [VERIFY] Derived, not supplied: $7,074 ÷ 2.22671% implies a taxable value near $317,700. No DCAD assessed value was provided for this parcel.
taxes.exemptions: [VERIFY] Not stated. The MLS figure is described as the unexempt amount.
taxes.specialAssessments: None disclosed. Public Improvement District (PID): No. Municipal Utility District (MUD): No.
taxes.melloRoos: Not applicable — Mello-Roos is a California mechanism and does not exist in Texas.
notes: The single most important tax point for a buyer: the $7,074 figure reflects the current taxable value, not the list price. Texas has no California-style Proposition 13 cap, and values are reappraised toward market. At the $485,000 list price the same combined rate produces roughly $10,800 a year — about $900 a month — which is an estimate, not a quote.

A buyer who occupies the home as a principal residence may be eligible to file a Texas homestead exemption, which would reduce the taxable value. Eligibility and amounts must be confirmed with DCAD. A buyer using the home as a short-term rental or second home would not qualify.
Assessed values are reviewed annually and can change through the appraisal review process.

highlights.title: A 1920 cottage, fully renovated
highlights.body: Craftsman-style trim, wood doors and herringbone-patterned floors carry the age of the house; the kitchen and bath are new work.

highlights.title: Turnkey, and furnished
highlights.body: The home is offered fully furnished, so a second-home or investment buyer can take it as it stands. What conveys is set out in the contract.

highlights.title: A kitchen built to use every inch
highlights.body: Large island, abundant cabinetry, stainless appliances, an apron-front sink, brass hardware and a gas range in an open plan with the living room.

highlights.title: A bath worth the square footage
highlights.body: Glass-enclosed walk-in shower with a built-in bench, subway tile, graphic black-and-white tilework, black fixtures and brass accents — in a room that measures 8 by 15.

highlights.title: Storage designed in, not added on
highlights.body: A custom closet system in the bedroom, two closets, and built-in cabinetry through the living room and bath.

highlights.title: Solar panels installed in 2023
highlights.body: A 2023 addition to the house. Ownership, production and transfer terms are part of the due-diligence package.

highlights.title: No HOA, and a lot you can actually maintain
highlights.body: No association, no assessment, no architectural committee — on a compact 0.053-acre lot with off-street parking on a concrete driveway and pad.

highlights.title: A proven short-term rental
highlights.body: The listing reports a successful run as a short-term rental. Permitting and the rules that apply at this address are a buyer's own due diligence — no income figures are published here.

marketing.headline: Small, and not one bit compromised
marketing.pullQuote: 744 square feet, renovated to the last inch, on a lot you can keep with a Saturday morning.
